name: Kareah
overview: Kareah was a male figure known primarily as the father of Johanan, one of the captains of the Judean forces during a critical period in Judah's history. Beyond his paternal role, little else is recorded about him, and his tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture. His mention is brief but situates him within the military leadership context of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Kareah means 'bald head' in Hebrew, indicating a proper name without a divine origin. This name is recorded in 2 Kings 25:23 and does not carry additional titles or meanings in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Kareah as the father of Johanan, a captain of the Judean forces, as noted in 2 Kings 25:23. He is also inferred to be the father of Jonathan, mentioned in Jeremiah 40:8. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Kareah's significance lies chiefly in his connection to his son Johanan, who played a notable role as a military leader during the turbulent final days of Judah. His mention anchors the leadership lineage present in the Judean resistance and survival efforts. Though Kareah himself is not a central figure, his familial link to key leaders highlights the continuity of faithful service amid national crisis.
